To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) A simple front-end based on a BLSTM and a subsequent beamforming operation can significantly reduce the word error rate for the CHiME 3 task; (2) A blind beamforming operation with BAN can outperform the best baseline system in the CHiME3 challenge, even when applied to real data; (3) Our approach can generalize well to real data, while being trained on simulated data; (4) A combination of our front-end with a language model

a) a simple, but well designed front-end is crucial for the success of an automatic speech recognition system, b) a bi-directional LSTM is a powerful tool for estimating soft masks for beamforming and c) beamforming is a promising tool for automatic speech recognition in the presence of interfering speakers and background noise.

(i) the combination of a BLSTM network with GEV beamformer is a powerful approach to improve speech enhancement for the 3rd CHiME challenge, (ii) this setup can easily be trained on simulated data and (iii) it can be used to obtain a very competitive result on the real data without any modification of the back end.

the development of an end-to-end speech enhancement system for noisy reverberant speech, which achieves state-of-the-art results on a challenging real data set.
a new front-end for speech enhancement and recognition that is based on a bi-directional LSTM network, which we call BLSTM-GEV.
the development of novel front-ends for speech separation and recognition.
